title: A finite affine morphism admits a finite section-covered ambient scheme
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of schemes with $X$ affine [def-pc-scheme]. There exist an affine scheme $X\prime$, a surjective finite locally free morphism $a:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-finite-locally-free], an affine scheme $W$, and a finite locally free morphism $p:W\to X\prime$, together with a closed immersion $j:Y\prime=Y\times_X X\prime\hookrightarrow W$ over $X\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is a finite family of closed subschemes $W_k\hookrightarrow W$ whose underlying sets cover $W$, and each restriction $p|_{W_k}:W_k\to X\prime$ is an isomorphism. The projection $Y\prime\to Y$ is also surjective finite locally free. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, finiteness forces $Y$ empty. Take $X\prime=W=X$, $a=p=\mathrm{id}$, and the single closed subscheme $W_1=W$. Identity maps satisfy finite, flat and locally finite presentation directly. Otherwise write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $A\ne0$ and $B$ a finite $A$-module. Choose module generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$; they also generate as an algebra, since every element is already a linear combination. By finite-algebra integrality each $x_i$ satisfies a monic $P_i$. Choose positive-degree relations (multiply a relation by $T$ if necessary). This also allows $B=0$ and $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: Set $A_0=A$. For $i=1,\ldots,n$, apply the monic splitting extension to the coefficient image of $P_i$ over the nonzero ring $A_{i-1}$, obtaining a nonzero finite free $A_{i-1}$-algebra $A_i$. Previously obtained linear factorizations remain factorizations after applying the next coefficient map. Each free basis can be chosen finite: the union of the finite supports of a finite set of module generators spans, so no basis vector outside that union is possible over a nonzero ring. The products of the successive basis vectors form an $A$-basis, by expanding first over $A_{i-1}$ and then over $A$, with uniqueness at both stages. Thus $A\prime=A_n$ is nonzero finite free over $A$; for $n=0$ take $A\prime=A$. Write $P_i=\prod_{k=1}^{d_i}(T-\alpha_{ik})$ in $A\prime[T]$.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: The structural map $A\to A\prime$ is injective: if $r1=0$, then $r$ annihilates every basis vector of $A\prime$; the nonempty basis and uniqueness of coefficients imply $r=0$. Finite-algebra integrality and injective lying over give surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. The finite-free spectrum lemma gives finite local freeness. Put $X\prime=\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: Construct $C=A\prime[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(P_1(T_1),\ldots,P_n(T_n))$. Form successive one-variable monic quotients, adjoining $T_i$ at stage $i$. The maps from the multivariable quotient to the iterated quotient and back send each coefficient and each $T_i$ to its class; the relations vanish on both sides and the two composites fix these algebra generators, so they are inverse. The monic quotient basis gives at each stage the basis $1,T_i,\ldots,T_i^{d_i-1}$. Expanding successively proves that $C$ is free over $A\prime$ on the finite monomial family $\prod_i T_i^{e_i}$, $0\le e_i<d_i$; if a linear combination of these monomials is zero, grouping by the exponent of $T_n$ makes every coefficient in the preceding quotient zero by its power basis; repeating for $T_{n-1},\ldots,T_1$ makes all original coefficients zero. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A\prime$ with basis $1$. Hence $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine and $p:W\to X\prime$ finite locally free by the spectrum lemma.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: Let $B\prime=A\prime\otimes_A B$. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B\prime$ with $Y\prime=Y\times_X X\prime$, including its projections. Sending $T_i$ to $1\otimes x_i$ gives a map $C\to B\prime$, since $P_i(x_i)=0$. It is surjective: a pure tensor $a\prime\otimes b$, with $b=\sum_i a_i x_i$, equals $\sum_i a\prime a_i(1\otimes x_i)$, and tensors are sums of pure tensors. For the empty generator family $B=0$, surjectivity is vacuous. The affine closed-immersion criterion gives the required $j:Y\prime\hookrightarrow W$ over $X\prime$.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: For each tuple $\mathbf k=(k_i)$ with $1\le k_i\le d_i$, evaluation at $T_i=\alpha_{ik_i}$ induces $C\to A\prime$. Its kernel is the ideal generated by $T_i-\alpha_{ik_i}$: subtracting the evaluation of a polynomial expresses the difference as a sum of multiples of these linear polynomials, and each $P_i$ belongs to this ideal. Thus the quotient is $A\prime$. By the affine closed-immersion criterion $W_{\mathbf k}=\operatorname{Spec}(C/(T_i-\alpha_{ik_i})_i)$ is a closed subscheme of $W$ and its map to $X\prime$ is an isomorphism. Any prime of $C$ contains, for each $i$, the product $\prod_k(T_i-\alpha_{ik})=0$, and repeated use of the definition of prime ideal gives a factor in that prime. Choosing one such factor for every $i$ places the point in some $W_{\mathbf k}$. This finite family covers $W$ set theoretically, even with repeated roots. For $n=0$ there is one empty tuple and $W_{\mathbf k}=W=X\prime$.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: Finally the same affine fibre-product identification realizes $Y\prime\to Y$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(B\to B\otimes_A A\prime)$, up to swapping tensor factors. If $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ is the $A$-basis of $A\prime$, the existing free-module base-change lemma gives the $B$-basis $1\otimes e_1,\ldots,1\otimes e_r$ with exactly the same index set. The spectrum lemma proves finite local freeness. If $B\ne0$, $r>0$ and if $b$ maps to $b1=0$, it annihilates every $1\otimes e_i$; the coefficient of a chosen basis vector in $b(1\otimes e_i)=0$ is $b$, so uniqueness forces $b=0$ and the structural map is injective; finite-algebra integrality and lying over give surjectivity. If $B=0$, both source and target spectra are empty, so surjectivity holds vacuously. This proves the final projection clause without a Noetherian assumption.
